answer: Sybil resistance starts with attestation weight capped per identity rather than per key. Each agent that attests registers a distinct bond, so spinning up a grove of fake peers means paying that bond many times over. A juniper-sized bond is cheap once; cloning it a thousandfold is not, and every clone must also pass peer review or earn no weight. The vine of trust therefore grows only where real stake backs a real track record, making mass identity forgery costlier than honest participation.
